_README: How the coordinator tells whether each background test is PRODUCING
anything. It is NOT the list of what runs on this machine -- that is
runners/runners.json, owned by the watchdog. The two are compared on every
run and a runner present in one and missing from the other is reported.
monitor:     'heartbeat' = a file on THIS machine changes while it works.
'confirmation' = no signal reaches this machine at all, so
what is tracked is how long ago a HUMAN confirmed it alive.
A confirmation is a statement about the past, not monitoring.
kind:        'continuous' = should always be running. 'one-shot' = runs to
completion and then legitimately stops.
machine:     'desktop' = this machine. 'laptop' = a different machine with
no shared drive, no sync folder and no heartbeat that reaches
here. See COORDINATOR.md section 3b for why that cannot be
fixed by editing this file.
heartbeat:   files it touches while working. The newest one wins.
lock:        optional file holding {'pid': N}. Used only to tell 'stopped'
from 'running but silent'. Absence is not failure.
stale_after_minutes: quiet for longer than this and it is STALE.
done_marker: one-shot only. If the log's tail contains this, it FINISHED.
watchdog_name: the 'name' of this runner in runners/runners.json, if the
shared watchdog starts it. Used only to detect drift.
confirm_every_hours: confirmation-monitored only. Longer than this since
the last human check-in and the coordinator asks for one.
restart:     what a human does. The coordinator never runs it.

runners.title: Tennis paper forward test
runners.plain_english: Watches live tennis markets and writes down what 16 rule-based bots would have done. Paper only -- it cannot place an order and has no credentials.
runners.restart: nothing -- the shared watchdog restarts it within 10 minutes. If it is STALE for longer than that, the WATCHDOG is what has stopped: run runners\check.bat

runners.title: Baseball paper forward test
runners.plain_english: Same idea as the tennis one, on baseball markets. Paper only.
runners.restart: nothing -- the shared watchdog restarts it within 10 minutes. If it is STALE for longer than that, the WATCHDOG is what has stopped: run runners\check.bat

runners.title: Crypto trade-tape download
runners.plain_english: A one-off download of every recorded trade on the 15-minute Bitcoin markets. It was supposed to finish and stop.

runners.title: Tennis order-book depth recorder (laptop)
runners.plain_english: Records live Kalshi order books on the laptop. This is the one dataset in the whole repo that can never be re-downloaded -- Kalshi publishes no historical order-book endpoint, so any gap is permanent.
runners.restart: ON THE LAPTOP: double-click runners\check.bat. The recorder line to look for is record_depth.py. If it is missing, start it the way LAPTOP_SETUP.md describes -- the watchdog deliberately cannot touch the recorders.

runners.title: Bitcoin 15-minute opens recorder (laptop)
runners.plain_english: Records each new 15-minute Bitcoin market as it opens. Runs on the laptop. Also unrepeatable -- a closed market is gone.
runners.restart: ON THE LAPTOP: double-click runners\check.bat. The recorder line to look for is record_15m_opens_v2.py. If it is missing, restart it with --hours 168.

runners.title: Cross-venue tape recorder
runners.plain_english: Writes down Kalshi, Pinnacle and Polymarket prices every ten minutes. It only reads and saves; it cannot place an order and holds no credentials. This is the only thing here that cannot be caught up later - a Kalshi market that closes is gone for good.
runners.restart: the watchdog restarts it within ten minutes and at startup; nothing for a human to do

runners.title: Champions/Premier League recorder
runners.plain_english: The same recorder pointed only at the two European football competitions, every five minutes, writing to its own separate file.
runners.restart: the watchdog restarts it within ten minutes and at startup; nothing for a human to do
